chapter_title: DBMS UNIT - I: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

questions.stem: How does Physical Data Independence benefit application software maintenance in an enterprise environment?

options.A: It enables modifying physical storage indexing or block layout without changing the conceptual schema or application code
options.B: It allows modifying conceptual tables without altering user SQL view definitions
options.C: It guarantees that concurrent transactions execute in serializable order without deadlock
options.D: It automatically converts non-relational unstructured data into third normal form

questions.explanation: Physical data independence insulates conceptual schemas and application programs from modifications made to physical disk storage structures, indexing methods, or page clustering.

questions.stem: In an Entity-Relationship diagram, when every entity in an entity set must participate in at least one relationship instance, what constraint is established?

options.A: Partial Participation represented by a single line
options.B: Disjoint Constraint represented by a circle with 'd'
options.C: Total Participation represented by a double line
options.D: Cardinality Constraint represented by an arrow

questions.explanation: Total participation (existence dependency) mandates that every entity in the entity set must participate in the relationship, visually denoted by a double line.

questions.stem: How is a Many-to-Many (M:N) binary relationship correctly translated into a relational database schema?

options.A: By embedding the primary key of either entity set as a foreign key in the other table
options.B: By creating a separate associative table whose composite primary key comprises foreign keys referencing both entity tables
options.C: By merging both entity tables into a single unified table with nullable columns
options.D: By adding multivalued array attributes to both entity relations

questions.explanation: In relational design, an M:N relationship cannot be represented via foreign key embedding without duplicating rows or violating 1NF. It requires an associative table with a composite primary key.

questions.stem: What is the primary key formulation for a Weak Entity Set during relational reduction?

options.A: The weak entity's partial discriminator key alone
options.B: A newly generated system surrogate integer column
options.C: The primary key of the identifying relationship set alone
options.D: The composite key combining the identifying owner entity's primary key and the weak entity's discriminator

questions.explanation: A weak entity table's primary key is formed by taking the primary key of its identifying owner entity and concatenating it with the weak entity's discriminator (partial key).

questions.stem: What foreign key action causes all child records to be automatically deleted when the referenced parent primary key row is deleted?
questions.explanation: The `ON DELETE CASCADE` referential action instructs the DBMS to automatically propagate deletions from the parent table to all referencing child tuples.

questions.stem: If relation R has degree 4 and cardinality 10, and relation S has degree 3 and cardinality 5, what are the degree and cardinality of the Cartesian Product (R × S)?
questions.explanation: For Cartesian Product $R \times S$, Degree $= \text{Deg}(R) + \text{Deg}(S) = 4 + 3 = 7$. Cardinality $= \text{Card}(R) \times \text{Card}(S) = 10 \times 5 = 50$.

questions.stem: What requirement must two relations satisfy before Set Union (∪) or Set Difference (-) can be evaluated between them?

options.B: They must be Union-Compatible, possessing identical degree and pairwise compatible attribute domains
options.C: They must share identical primary key column names
options.D: They must both reside on the same physical storage volume

questions.explanation: Set operations require union compatibility: both relations must have the same number of attributes (same degree), and corresponding attributes must have compatible domains.

questions.stem: In Extended ER (EER) modeling, what does a disjointness constraint labeled 'd' enforce across subclasses?

options.A: Every superclass entity must belong to at least one subclass
options.B: Subclasses do not inherit the attributes of the superclass
options.C: An entity instance can be a member of at most one subclass within the specialization hierarchy
options.D: Entities in subclasses can exist without an identifying superclass instance

questions.explanation: The disjoint constraint ($d$) enforces mutual exclusion among subclasses: an entity cannot belong to more than one subclass in that specialization.

questions.stem: How is a Multivalued Attribute resolved during relational schema translation to preserve First Normal Form (1NF)?

options.A: By creating a dedicated relation containing the multivalued attribute and the owner's primary key as a composite key
options.B: By allocating five static columns (e.g., Phone1, Phone2, Phone3) in the base relation
options.C: By storing the values as a comma-delimited string in the base relation
options.D: By converting the attribute into an external view definition

questions.explanation: To satisfy 1NF atomicity, multivalued attributes are extracted into a separate table with a composite primary key consisting of the owner's primary key and the attribute value.

questions.stem: Which of the following database view definitions is inherently NON-UPDATABLE under standard SQL rules?

options.A: A view selecting three columns from a single table with a WHERE condition
options.B: A view selecting all columns of a table without any WHERE condition
options.C: A view created with the WITH CHECK OPTION clause over a single table
options.D: A view containing an aggregate function (AVG, SUM) and a GROUP BY clause

questions.explanation: Views containing aggregate functions, `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT`, or joins cannot be directly updated because modifications cannot be mapped unambiguously to base table tuples.
